userStories.title: Ingest the write-path lines
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Parse the five new runner write-path stream lines and `session_started.stale`, and fold them into the ChatThread columns and session snapshot.

**Motivation** — The API's stream parser currently counts the five C1 line types as bad lines, so write results never reach the thread.

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

New parsed line types in `thread-line.ts` (each with optional `at`, kept like the session lines):

| Line | Valid when | Parsed |
|---|---|---|
| `write_doc` | `path` non-empty string of at most 512 characters, `bytes` integer >= 0 | `{ type, at?, path, bytes }` |
| `published` | `sha` 40 or 64 lowercase hex, `paths` and `ignored` arrays of at most 200 strings of 1..512 characters, `specPresent` boolean | `{ type, at?, sha, paths, ignored, specPresent }` |
| `publish_failed` | `reason` non-empty string of at most 64 characters | `{ type, at?, reason }` |
| `discarded` | `tipSha` 40 or 64 lowercase hex | `{ type, at?, tipSha }` |
| `discard_failed` | `reason` non-empty string of at most 64 characters | `{ type, at?, reason }` |
| `session_started` | as today; `stale` absent or `true` (any other value -> bad) | adds `stale: true` only when the line has it |

Fold (new `ingest/thread-write-fold.ts`, called from `fold` under the existing job and thread locks; `at` = the line's `at` or the fold's clock, `jobId` = the batch's job). It exports a pure function, testable without a database:

`fold` reads the thread's `writtenPaths` and `session`, calls `writeLinePatch`, and writes the patch with one `chatThread.update`. Every write-path line marks the thread changed, so the fold emits the existing `thread` live event:

| Line | `ChatThread` update |
|---|---|
| `write_doc` | append `path` to `writtenPaths` unless already present; when `writtenPaths` already holds 200 entries the path is not added |
| `published` | `publishedSha = sha`, `specPublished = specPresent`, `writtenPaths = []`, `lastWrite = { kind: 'published', jobId, at, sha, paths, ignored }` |
| `publish_failed` | `lastWrite = { kind: 'publish_failed', jobId, at, reason }`; `writtenPaths` unchanged |
| `discarded` | `writtenPaths = []`, `lastWrite = { kind: 'discarded', jobId, at, sha: tipSha }`, and the stored session loses its `stale` key when it has one |
| `discard_failed` | `lastWrite = { kind: 'discard_failed', jobId, at, reason }` |

`foldSessionLine` writes `stale: true` into the stored session only when the `session_started` line has it. `ThreadSession` (chat-thread.domain.ts:16) adds optional `stale?: true`; `ThreadDto.session` OpenAPI `properties` (threads/dto/thread.dto.ts:25) adds `stale` (boolean) — run `bun run generate` at the repo root. The parsed `session_started` line gains `stale` only when the input has it, so existing `toEqual` assertions stay valid. `parseThreadLine` is at thread-line.ts:207; `PrismaThreadIngestRepository.fold` at prisma-thread-ingest.repository.ts:69.

**Scope** — In: thread-line.ts parsing, ingest/thread-write-fold.ts, fold wiring, ThreadSession.stale, ThreadDto.session OpenAPI stale property. Out: the THREAD_PUBLISH rejected-ack write (US-004), Publish/Discard routes (US-003/US-004), Plan gating on specPublished (US-006).

**Interface**
```ts
export type WriteLine = Extract<ThreadLine, { type: 'write_doc' | 'published' | 'publish_failed' | 'discarded' | 'discard_failed' }>;
export interface WriteFoldState { writtenPaths: string[]; session: ThreadSession | null }
export interface WriteFoldPatch { writtenPaths?: string[]; publishedSha?: string; specPublished?: boolean; lastWrite?: ThreadWriteResult; session?: ThreadSession }
/** The `ChatThread` fields one write-path line changes; keys it does not change are absent. */
export function writeLinePatch(state: WriteFoldState, line: WriteLine, ctx: { jobId: string; at: string }): WriteFoldPatch;
```
acceptanceCriteria: parseThreadLine('{"type":"write_doc","path":"docs/a.md","bytes":12}') returns { type: 'write_doc', path: 'docs/a.md', bytes: 12 }
parseThreadLine of a write_doc line with bytes: -1 returns { bad: true }

parseThreadLine of a published line with a 40-hex sha S, paths: ['docs/a.md'], ignored: [] and specPresent: true returns { type: 'published', sha: S, paths: ['docs/a.md'], ignored: [], specPresent: true }
parseThreadLine of a published line whose sha is 'xyz' returns { bad: true }
parseThreadLine('{"type":"publish_failed","reason":"branch_moved"}') returns { type: 'publish_failed', reason: 'branch_moved' }
parseThreadLine of a discarded line with a 40-hex tipSha T returns { type: 'discarded', tipSha: T }
parseThreadLine of a session_started line with resumed: false and stale: true returns a line whose stale is true
parseThreadLine of a session_started line with resumed: false and stale: false returns { bad: true }
Folding two write_doc lines for docs/a.md and one for docs/b.md leaves the thread's writtenPaths equal to ['docs/a.md', 'docs/b.md']

Folding a published line with sha S, specPresent: true, paths: ['docs/a.md'] and ignored: [] on a thread with writtenPaths ['docs/a.md'] leaves the thread with { publishedSha: S, specPublished: true, writtenPaths: [], lastWrite: { kind: 'published', jobId: <batch job>, at: <line at>, sha: S, paths: ['docs/a.md'], ignored: [] } }
Folding a publish_failed line with reason 'branch_moved' and at A sets the thread's lastWrite to { kind: 'publish_failed', jobId: <batch job>, at: A, reason: 'branch_moved' }

Folding a discarded line with tipSha T on a thread whose writtenPaths is ['docs/a.md'] and whose stored session has stale: true leaves the thread with writtenPaths: [], lastWrite.kind 'discarded', lastWrite.sha T and a stored session without a stale key

routing.reasoning: Extends an existing parser and fold with one new pure module (writeLinePatch) under the existing locks; no new abstractions or access control, so the light strategy suffices.

userStories.title: Discard, the publish ack and the write_doc instructions
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `POST .../discard`, record rejected `THREAD_PUBLISH` acks into `lastWrite`, refuse stop/end-session during action jobs, and tell the agent about `write_doc`.

**Motivation** — Discard clears a stale session's unpublished changes, a rejected publish must be visible to the page, and `buildThreadInstructions` still says 'You cannot write files in this session'.

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

`POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/discard` (creator, users only, 200, body `{}`, returns `{ jobId: string }`). Same locks; checks in order: 404 / 403 as Publish; `threads.disabled`; `threads.archived`; `thread.runnerId` null -> 409 `threads.nothingToDiscard`; `threads.runnerOffline`; `threads.runnerOutdated` and the budget pause (as Publish step 4); any active job of the thread, including a live session -> 409 `threads.busy`; otherwise `createThreadJob(thread, 'DISCARD')`, place it after commit, return `{ jobId }`. The budget-pause refusal is the same as Publish step 4 (`BudgetPausedException`, 409 `fleet.budgetPaused`). `createThreadJob` (created by US-003) sets `maxCostUsd` to the fixed string `'0'` for `PUBLISH` / `DISCARD`.

A `THREAD_PUBLISH` ack (`ThreadJobEffects.onInputAck`, threads/thread-job-effects.ts:23; `CommandAckProcessor` routes it there, fleet/sync/command-ack.processor.ts:68-69) with result `rejected` sets `lastWrite = { kind: 'publish_failed', jobId: command.jobId, at: <now>, reason: <ack detail, at most 64 characters> }`, except when the detail is `publishing` (a second click while the first publish runs; its own result line follows and must not be overwritten); an `ok` ack writes nothing (the `published` line follows on the stream).

C2-D7: while a thread's active `THREAD` job is a `PUBLISH` or `DISCARD` job, stop and end-session (through `PrismaChatThreadRepository.command`) answer 409 `threads.noSession`, because there is no session to act on. Answer keeps its existing order and answers `threads.noQuestion`. `PrismaChatThreadRepository.command` answers 409 `threads.noSession` for `THREAD_STOP_TURN` and `THREAD_CLOSE` when the current `THREAD` job's `FleetThreadTurn.action` is `PUBLISH` or `DISCARD`; the check runs where the existing `noSession` check runs, after the `THREAD_ANSWER` question check.

`buildThreadInstructions` (thread-instructions.ts:3) replaces step 2's "You cannot write files in this session. Put the spec draft in your reply." and the tools line's "no write access" with:

- step 2: `When the person agrees the intent is settled, call load_skill with "spec-writing" if it is listed below and follow it. Write the spec to <specPath> with write_doc.`
- a new line after the tools line: `write_doc writes Markdown (.md) files under docs/ and .nax/features/<feature>/ only. Nothing is committed until the person presses Publish; tell them when a draft is ready to publish.`
- the tools line becomes: `Tools: list_files and search_repo find files and text; read files with your read tool; write_doc writes docs. You have no shell and no web access.`

i18n: add `nothingToDiscard` "Thread has nothing to discard" to both `apps/api/src/i18n/en/threads.json` and `apps/api/src/i18n/zh/threads.json`.

Symbol changes: `ThreadJobEffects.onInputAck` also handles `THREAD_PUBLISH`; `ChatThreadRepository` adds `discard(projectId, threadId, userId)`; controller/service route. In `thread-instructions.spec.ts` the existing AC3 asserts `Put the spec draft in your reply.`, which this story removes: replace it with an assertion that the instructions name `write_doc` and the spec path, and keep AC1, AC2 and AC4. Add the discard route's happy path and one refusal (`threads.busy`) to the threads block of `apps/api/test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts` (existing tests unchanged). Run `bun run generate` at the repo root.

**Scope** — In: discard route, publish ack handling, noSession for action jobs, instructions text, nothingToDiscard i18n. Out: the Publish route and createThreadJob extraction (US-003), Plan/Run (US-006/US-007), ingest folding of `discarded` lines (US-002).

```ts
discard(projectId: string, threadId: string, userId: string): Promise<{ jobId: string }>;
// ThreadJobEffects.onInputAck additionally handles FleetCommandType.THREAD_PUBLISH
```

userStories.title: Runner PLAN expectBranch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the optional PLAN-only ASSIGN field `expectBranch`: the runner fails a PLAN whose PRD names a different branch and makes a thread PLAN start from the local branch.

**Motivation** — A thread's re-published docs are ahead of `origin/<branch>` after the first PLAN pushed, and a PLAN whose PRD names the wrong branch must not push.

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

- `AssignPayload.expectBranch?: string` — "PLAN only: the branch the PRD must name (a thread PLAN)" (packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts:230).
- `parseAssign` (apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts): `expectBranch` present on a non-`PLAN` job -> `invalid expectBranch`; on a `PLAN` it must pass the same `plain(..., 255)` rule as `ref` (else `invalid expectBranch`) and is copied; absent -> the parsed assign has no `expectBranch` key.
- `checkPlanPrd(text, expectBranch?)` (apps/runner/src/verdict/plan-verdict.ts:11): after the existing checks, when `expectBranch` is given and `prd.branchName !== expectBranch`, the result is `{ ok: false, reason: 'branch_mismatch', branchName: prd.branchName }`.
- `HostExecutor.readPlan(job)` (executor/host-executor.ts:201) passes `job.assign.expectBranch`, so `planVerdict` (verdict/plan-verdict.ts:19, called from supervisor/job-run.ts:412-414) ends the job `FAILED` with reason `branch_mismatch` and `finishPlan` (host-executor.ts:217) pushes nothing (its existing `!check.ok` refusal).
- `prepareCheckout` (executor/checkout.ts:17) for a `PLAN` with `expectBranch`: when `refs/heads/<expectBranch>` exists in the clone, the checkout detaches at that local commit (a thread's re-published docs are ahead of `origin/<branch>` after the first PLAN pushed); otherwise the existing `resolveRef(assign.ref)` path (executor/refs.ts:11, origin first). The `.nax` check applies to whichever commit is chosen.

`checkPlanPrd`'s new parameter is optional and the parsed assign gains `expectBranch` only when the ASSIGN has it, so the existing `verdict.spec.ts`, `job-run.spec.ts` and assign-parser tests stay valid. `FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 4; older runners ignore the field. Also run `bun run type-check` at the repo root.

**Scope** — In: AssignPayload.expectBranch, parseAssign, checkPlanPrd, readPlan, prepareCheckout. Out: the API setting `expectBranch` in `buildAssignPayload` (US-006), any API change.

**Interface**
```ts
// packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts
interface AssignPayload { /* ... */ /** PLAN only: the branch the PRD must name (a thread PLAN) */ expectBranch?: string }
// verdict/plan-verdict.ts
function checkPlanPrd(text: string, expectBranch?: string): /* existing result */ | { ok: false; reason: 'branch_mismatch'; branchName: string }
```

userStories.title: Run from a thread
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add `POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/run`, dispatching the thread's `RUN` job after its latest PLAN completed.

**Motivation** — Closing the loop on the API so that C3 only adds buttons: Run must follow a completed Plan on `feat/<feature>` under the same one-active-job rule.

**Approach** — verbatim from the spec:

`POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/run` (creator, users only, 201, body `RunThreadDto { profiles?; maxCostUsd?: number; bashMode?: 'raw' | 'gated' | 'escalate' }`), with the same `CREATE FleetJob` ability check (403 `projects`) and the same `maxCostUsd` default (`THREAD_HANDOFF_DEFAULT_MAX_COST_USD = 5`) as Plan (US-006). `ThreadsService.run` checks in order: 404 / 403; `threads.disabled`; `threads.archived`; the thread's latest `PLAN` job is missing or not `COMPLETED` -> 409 `threads.notPlanned`; then `dispatch(..., { repoId, command: 'RUN', ref: 'feat/<feature>', feature, profiles, maxCostUsd, bashMode, pinnedRunnerId: thread.runnerId }, { threadId })`. The latest PLAN is the thread's job of command PLAN ordered `queuedAt desc, id desc` (the same query `handoff` uses). `RunThreadDto` goes next to `PlanThreadDto` in `threads/dto/thread-handoff.dto.ts`. A RUN job has `planFrom` null and its ASSIGN has no `expectBranch` key (buildAssignPayload adds it only for a PLAN with a threadId). The thread detail `handoff.run` (US-006) reports the new job.

i18n: add `notPlanned` "The thread's latest plan has not completed" to both `apps/api/src/i18n/en/threads.json` and `apps/api/src/i18n/zh/threads.json`.

Add the run route's `threads.notPlanned` refusal and its happy path after a `COMPLETED` PLAN to the threads block of `apps/api/test/e2e/api-endpoint/endpoint.e2e.spec.ts` (existing tests unchanged). Run `bun run generate` at the repo root.

**Scope** — In: run route/service, RunThreadDto, notPlanned i18n. Out: dispatch threadId option, lockIdleThread, handoff and expectBranch (US-006); Run does not re-check spec re-publication.

**Interface**
```ts
// threads/dto/thread-handoff.dto.ts
class RunThreadDto { profiles?: string[]; maxCostUsd?: number; bashMode?: 'raw' | 'gated' | 'escalate' }
```
acceptanceCriteria: POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/run with {} on a thread whose latest PLAN job is COMPLETED and with no active job creates a RUN job whose { ref, feature, pinnedRunnerId, threadId, planFrom } equal { 'feat/<feature>', <thread feature>, <thread runnerId>, <thread id>, null }
POST .../run on a thread with no PLAN job answers 409 threads.notPlanned
POST .../run on a thread whose latest PLAN job is FAILED and whose earlier PLAN job is COMPLETED answers 409 threads.notPlanned
POST .../run with { bashMode: 'escalate', profiles: ['native'] } creates a RUN job whose { bashMode, profiles } equal { 'escalate', ['native'] }
POST .../run while a RUN job with the thread's threadId is RUNNING answers 409 threads.busy
Given a RUN job created by POST .../run on a thread whose latest PLAN job is COMPLETED, the ASSIGN that PlacementService builds for it has no expectBranch key
POST .../run by a project member who is not the creator answers 403 threads.notCreator
GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id after POST .../run created a RUN job returns handoff.run.jobId equal to that job's id

routing.reasoning: Small mirror of Plan, but creator-only and ability-gated endpoint (security override).

suggestedCriteria: POST .../run with {} creates a job whose maxCostUsd is 5
outOfScope: US-007 only: the `CREATE FleetJob` ability check and the `maxCostUsd` default share Plan's rules (US-006), and Run's `bashMode` validation and `threads.disabled` / `threads.archived` share Plan's rules without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

modifiedFiles.reason: add the run route's `threads.notPlanned` refusal and its happy path after a `COMPLETED` PLAN to the threads block; existing tests are unchanged.

analysis:
Feature C2 of fleet S5a phase C. C1 (fleet-s5a-thread-write, #268) merged the runner write path (write_doc, Publish, stale start, Discard) and fleet-protocol types (ThreadAction, ThreadAssign.title?, ThreadRunnerLine, ThreadPublishFailReason, ThreadDiscardFailReason, RunnerCapabilities.threadWrite?). Nothing reaches them from the API yet. C2 wires the API: publish/discard/plan/run routes, ingest of five new runner stream lines plus session_started.stale, threadWrite capability parsing and placement, one-active-job-per-thread rule, write_doc instructions; plus one runner story (PLAN expectBranch).

Key files (API): apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma (ChatThread ~L1057); fleet/common/capabilities-core.ts (parseCapabilitiesCore, configJobs strict pattern); fleet/jobs/placement-rules.ts (PlacementJob.thread, MisfitReason, firstMisfit, toPlacementJob); fleet/jobs/placement.service.ts (placeJob, fillRunnerThreads, private assign, budget-pause cancel at ~L70); fleet/jobs/prisma-fleet-job.repository.ts (findThreadAssign ~L192, createJob); fleet/jobs/assign-payload.ts (buildAssignPayload); fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.ts (dispatch ~L63); fleet/jobs/domain/fleet-job.domain.ts (IFleetJobRepository ~L198, NewFleetJob.threadId ~L115); fleet/threads/* (prisma-chat-thread.repository.ts sendMessage/command/currentThreadJob/mapThread, threads.service.ts, threads.controller.ts, thread-send-rules.ts, thread-instructions.ts, thread-job-effects.ts, domain/chat-thread.domain.ts); fleet/threads/ingest/{thread-line.ts,prisma-thread-ingest.repository.ts}; fleet/sync/command-ack.processor.ts (routes THREAD_INPUT/THREAD_ANSWER at ~L68); i18n en/zh threads.json (409 key shape { key: { "409": text } }); DTO enums at fleet/jobs/dto/fleet-job.dto.ts:107 and dashboard/dashboard.types.ts:109 (MISFIT_REASONS) gain thread_write.
Runner: apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts, verdict/plan-verdict.ts (checkPlanPrd, planVerdict), executor/checkout.ts (prepareCheckout), executor/refs.ts (resolveRef), executor/host-executor.ts (readPlan/finishPlan), supervisor/job-run.ts:412-414; packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts (AssignPayload ~L230).

Binding rulings: C2-R1 one feature, expectBranch optional so older runners ignore it. C2-D1 write results live in ChatThread.lastWrite, stale lives on session snapshot. C2-D2 one-active-job rule counts every non-terminal FleetJob with the threadId; for PLAN/RUN checked in dispatch's transaction under a ChatThread row lock (lockIdleThread). C2-D3 PUBLISH/DISCARD skip backend check, require threadWrite; thread_write is not a PERMANENT_MISFIT; routes refuse paused budget scope with BudgetPausedException up front. C2-D4 ThreadJobEffects.onJobEnded unchanged. C2-D5 live-session Publish allowed with empty writtenPaths; no-session Publish requires non-empty. C2-D6 PLAN/RUN use ref feat/<feature>, pinnedRunnerId = thread.runnerId, PLAN planFrom = specPath, ASSIGN of thread PLAN carries expectBranch = job.ref. C2-D7 stop/end-session answer threads.noSession while the active THREAD job is PUBLISH/DISCARD.

Risks: (1) Concurrency: Plan/Run lock via SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside the dispatch txManager; sendMessage/publish use job-then-thread lock order with retry; keep lock order consistent to avoid deadlocks. (2) createThreadJob extraction from sendMessage must preserve today's behaviour (feature thread-<id>, ref baseRef, pinnedRunnerId, bashMode raw, DuplicateActiveJobError mapping) — existing tests in thread-send-guards e2e must stay valid. PUBLISH/DISCARD maxCostUsd is the string '0' (must pass runner COST_RE nax-process.ts:7). (3) Backward compat: parseThreadLine gains stale only when present so existing toEqual assertions hold; placement test fixtures omit action and must behave as SESSION; ThreadSession.stale optional. (4) Migration is additive only (4 columns with defaults). (5) Generated artifacts: stories adding routes/DTO fields must run `bun run generate` at repo root (openapi.json and apps/cli/src/generated are committed; never hand-edit generated files). (6) API DB-backed specs need `bun run test:db:up` and KODA_DB_TESTS=1; the agent shell has no docker. (7) i18n: add every new 409 key to both en and zh threads.json in the story that first throws it (busy, nothingToPublish: US-003; nothingToDiscard: US-004; notPublished: US-006; notPlanned: US-007). (8) The existing thread-instructions.spec.ts AC3 asserts text removed by US-004 and must be replaced. (9) apps/api lints with oxlint; immutability preferred (no mutating arrays/objects), small files.
Tests: unit *.spec.ts beside source, integration under apps/api/test/integration/fleet/, e2e under apps/api/test/e2e (endpoint.e2e.spec.ts must get each new endpoint's happy path and one refusal). Runner uses bun:test.
Dependency order: US-001 and US-005 first (independent); US-002 and US-003 after US-001; US-004 after US-003; US-006 after US-002, US-003, US-005; US-007 after US-006.
outOfScope: The web side of phase C (action bar, Discard banner, commit markers, PLAN / RUN cards) belongs to feature C3.
ACP thread backends belong to phase D; nothing in C2 depends on the backend kind.
The API never pushes or reads git; the runner commits on Publish and the thread's PLAN pushes `feat/<feature>`.
`FLEET_PROTOCOL_VERSION` stays 4; `expectBranch` is optional and an older runner ignores it (no `branch_mismatch`).
Base-ref drift is not rebased and a thread cannot move to another runner.
A rejected `THREAD_PUBLISH` ack writes `lastWrite` but emits no live event; the page sees it on its next thread refetch.
The thread detail's `sendRefusal` does not report `busy`; it stays `sendRefusal()`'s value, and C3 disables the composer from `activeJob` / `handoff` instead.
`RunnerSummaryDto` does not expose `threadWrite`; the write routes answer `threads.runnerOutdated` instead.
Plan and Run read `specPublished`, `status` and the latest PLAN before `dispatch` takes the thread lock; a thread archived or re-published in that window is not re-checked under the lock.
Run does not check whether the spec was re-published after the latest PLAN completed; it runs the PRD on the branch. C3 may warn about it.
A `PUBLISH` or `DISCARD` job re-adopted after a daemon restart ends `FAILED` (C1 behaviour); the API folds nothing for it.
The runner `context.md` and the API `context.md` are updated by hand after merge.

US-002 only: an `at` that is not an ISO date on a write-path line, a `published.paths` entry over 512 characters, a 64-hex `sha`, a malformed `publish_failed` / `discarded` line, the `discard_failed` line (parsed and folded like `publish_failed`), `writtenPaths` left unchanged by `publish_failed`, and a `session_started` without `stale` storing no `stale` key (already pinned by the existing fold tests) share the Design tables without a dedicated acceptance criterion.
US-003 only: Publish answering `threads.runnerOffline` for an offline runner (the same `isRunnerOnline` check Send uses) has no dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-003 only: Publish answering `threads.turnRunning` for a `QUEUED` / `ASSIGNED` session job or a `pending` message, `threads.closing` for an `UPLOADING` job, `threads.disabled` / `threads.archived`, and the budget-pause refusal share the Design steps (and `sendRefusal`'s existing tests) without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-003 only: the `{ jobId: null }` body of a live Publish and the `{ jobId }` body of a `PUBLISH` job, the job's `threadId` and `pinnedRunnerId` (set by the extracted `createThreadJob` exactly as `sendMessage` sets them today), a refused request creating no command or job, and 403 `threads.principal` for an agent API key (the controller's existing `assertUser`) share the Design rules without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-003 only: the job-then-thread lock order, the retry when the current job changes between the pre-lock read and the lock (as `sendMessage` retries today), and the `job.dispatched` activity row of a `PUBLISH` job share `sendMessage`'s existing behaviour without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-004 only: `threads.disabled`, `threads.archived`, `threads.runnerOffline` and the budget pause on Discard follow Publish's Design steps, stop answering `threads.noSession` shares end-session's rule (C2-D7), and an ack `detail` longer than 64 characters is cut to 64, without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-005 only: `expectBranch` failing the `plain` rule on a `PLAN`, the `.nax` check on the local commit, and `planVerdict` turning the `branch_mismatch` check into `FAILED` (its existing `!ok` path) share the rules in Design without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-006 only: 403 `threads.notCreator` on Plan (the same creator check as Publish, US-003 AC-13), `handoff.plan` picking the latest of several PLAN jobs (`queuedAt desc, id desc`, as `currentThreadJob` orders today), the losing request of two concurrent Plans answering 409 `threads.busy`, a `DuplicateActiveJobError` under `opts.threadId` keeping 409 `fleet.jobs`, `threads.disabled` and `threads.archived` on Plan, the `profiles` / `maxCostUsd` DTO bounds and `dispatch`'s budget gate share existing behaviour without a dedicated acceptance criterion.

US-007 only: the `CREATE FleetJob` ability check and the `maxCostUsd` default share Plan's rules (US-006), and Run's `bashMode` validation and `threads.disabled` / `threads.archived` share Plan's rules without a dedicated acceptance criterion.
